newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sideways after fall, gas oil spread weak.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sideways after fall, gas oil spread weak.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures traded sideways after an early fall on Wednesday after U.S. data released overnight showed rising inventories of gasoline and distillates last week, brokers said.
Jan Brent stood 15 cents lower at $23.62 per barrel by 1218 GMT.
Overall U.S. crude inventories fell 868,000 barrels last week, according to American Petroleum Institute data, but gasoline and distillate grew by 1.9 and 1.8 million barrels respectively.
However, the nationwide data hid significant regional variations, brokers said.
In the key northeast United States, distillates containing more than 0.05 percent sulphur, which is mostly heating oil, fell 1.2 million barrels in the week to stand 12.5 million below last year.
But brokers said gas oil was still under pressure from oversupply in the Rotterdam market following November's record delivery into the IPE contract.
"Gas oil is reluctant to follow the strength in other markets. A lot of the weakness is a hangover from the IPE delivery," a broker said.
Dec gas oil was 25 cents down at $222.50 per tonne and the Dec/Jan spread shed $1.25 from Tuesday to $1.75 backwardation.
"There's a lot of liquidation of the spread," a broker said, noting that it was trading at $4.00 on Friday.
